text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - A Philippine flour mill bought 17,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for November shipment. The deal was for 8,500 tonnes of 14 percent dark northern spring at $4.10 per bushel and 8,500 tonnes of western white at $4.00 per bushel. CORN TENDER - Taiwan will tender on Thursday for two 54,000-tonne shipments of U.S. corn. The first shipment was for December 10-25 FOB U.S. Gulf. The second shipment was for January 10-25 from the U.S. Gulf or January 26 to February 9 from the Pacific Northwest, they said.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - The Egyptian state's Food Industries Company said on Wednesday it was extending until noon (1000 GMT) on November 6 the deadline for bids for 30,000 tonnes U.S. or Argentine yellow corn and 30,000 tonnes of soybeans, any origin. The old deadline was October 30.

SOYMEAL TENDER - South Korean feed mill companies including Miwon Co Ltd, Woo Sung Feed Mill Co Ltd and Purina Korea passed on tenders for 15,500 tonnes of Indian soymeal due to high prices, traders said. Shipment had been set for December 20 to January 20 and arrival was slated for Kunsan.
BARLEY TENDER - The Cyprus Grain Commission said it invited tenders by October 29 for 25,000 tonnes feed barley for Nov 20-Dec 5 shipment from Europe or Nov 10-25 from North America.

WHEAT TENDER - Algeria is seeking 75,000 extra tonnes of soft wheat of French and/or Argentine origin in three lots of 25,000 tonnes each, trading sources said. Shipments are set for November and December. The tender expires on Thursday.

- Egypt's official commodities buyer said on Tuesday he was inviting bids for 50,000 tonnes of soft red French wheat or soft white standard wheat from Australia for delivery between November 1 and 15. The deadline for bids was Friday.

VEGOIL TENDER - Tunisia will tender on Thursday for up to 12,000 tonnes of soy and/or rapeseed oil for December 1996 and January 1997 delivery, the state-buying body Office National de l'Huile said. The tender was for one or two lots of 3,000 or 6,000 tonnes to be delivered December 5-20, 1996, and one or two lots of 3,000 or 6,000 tonnes for delivery January 5-20, 1997. Delivery is at two of the following three Tunisian ports -- La Goulette, Sousse and Sfax.

RICE TENDER - The Japanese Food Agency said on Monday it would buy 110,000 tonnes of rice at its import tender on October 24 and 10,000 tonnes at its November 8 tender. Under a 1993 agreement under the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, Japan agreed to gradually open its rice market and committed to import 511,000 tonnes of rice through March 1997.
MARKET TALK - Jordan has suspended a 16-percent customs duty for a six-month trial period in an attempt to encourage private sugar and rice purchases, officials and traders said.

... Falling U.S. grains and oilseeds may stabilize soon, disappointing Southeast Asian buyers who have stepped away from the market on expectations of a further fall in U.S. corn and soybean values, regional traders said.
... Sri Lanka plans to import more than 500,000 tonnes of its main staple rice this year to meet a shortfall caused by severe drought and rising demand, a senior food official said.
